commitResults.messageBody:
An edit whose new values all match the current ones still saves the
contact and reports success, which misleads the user into thinking
something changed.

Let's reject such edits with an error message and leave the contact
list unchanged, as specified in UC04 (extension 2e).

commitResults.messageTitle: Edit command: Reject phone or email used by others
commitResults.messageBody:
Editing a contact can give it the phone number or email of another
contact. Phone numbers and emails are meant to identify one contact
each, so such an edit creates two records for what may be the same
person.

Let's reject the whole edit when the new phone number or email
already belongs to another contact, naming that contact, as
specified in UC04 (extension 2c). Emails are compared case-
insensitively, since letter case does not change the address.

Only edited fields are checked, so contacts whose existing details
already clash can still have their other fields edited.

commitResults.messageTitle: Edit command: Allow choosing the contact by name
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit command only accepts an index, so the user has to list or
find a contact first to learn its number. UC04 and the UI mock-up
let the user name the contact instead.

Let's accept all or part of a name in place of the index, ignoring
case:
* one matching contact is edited directly
* several matches are listed with numbers, and nothing is edited;
  the list stays shown so the user can re-enter the command with an
  index from it
* no match shows that the contact was not found

The index form is kept as the one-shot way to pick among several
matches. A preamble whose first word is a number is still treated as
an index, so typos like "edit 1 foo" keep failing as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden clear command against extra arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
The clear command was routed straight from AddressBookParser to a
ClearCommand with no argument parsing, so `clear 3` silently wiped the
whole address book. It also gave the same message whether it cleared one
contact or none at all.

Add a ClearCommandParser that rejects any argument and shows the command
usage, report the number of contacts cleared on success, and report that
there is nothing to clear when the address book is already empty.

Confirmation prompts (UC05 steps 2-3) and save-failure handling (UC05
extension 4a) are left for a later iteration, as both need infrastructure
that does not exist yet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageBody:
The team decided Astra keeps AB3's command syntax: bare command words and

such as `/add` and `/delete`, and the Developer Guide glossary defined a

commitResults.messageTitle: Rework Person model for Astra's contact fields
commitResults.messageBody:
AB3's person carried a name, phone, email and address. Astra captures
people met at networking events, where the useful details are who someone
works for and what they do, and where an address is never collected.

Replace the address with a company, a role and a LinkedIn profile, and make
every field other than the name optional: a contact is often captured with
only a name and whatever was exchanged before the conversation moved on, so
requiring a phone and an email would make the app unusable for its own
purpose. Optional fields are nullable internally and exposed as Optional,
so callers cannot read an absent value by accident.

Identity is unchanged for now: two persons are still duplicates when their
names match. Keying on the contact number or email instead, and allowing
several values per field, are both later changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Hold contact fields to the rules the DG specifies
commitResults.messageBody:
Three gaps between the model and our own Developer Guide:

Normalisation. The glossary defines a display value as the normalised
spelling that Astra stores and shows, with outer spaces trimmed and
repeated spaces collapsed. Only the parsers trimmed, so "John  Doe" was
stored with two spaces and a value loaded straight from the save file was
never tidied at all. Add StringUtil#normalise and apply it in every field's
constructor, so a value is normalised wherever it enters the model.

Names. NFR 9 requires names containing non-English letters, but the
validation regex used the ASCII-only \p{Alnum}, so "Jose Garcia" was
rejected. Match Unicode letters and numbers instead, and allow the hyphens,
apostrophes and full stops that ordinary names contain.

Phone numbers. The glossary describes digits with optional balanced
parentheses and at least three digits; the regex accepted bare digits only,
so "+65 9312 1534" was rejected. Accept spaces, hyphens, a leading plus and
balanced parentheses, while still requiring three digits and rejecting
anything else. Parentheses are checked by counting depth rather than by
regex, so an unbalanced "(65 9312" is caught.

Two existing assertions change meaning as a result: an email with outer
spaces and a name with trailing spaces are now normalised rather than
rejected, which is what the glossary asks for and what the parsers already
did before validating.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Conflict in the Developer Guide glossary, where both sides edited adjacent

rules, and master rewrote the Prefix entry in #56. Kept both.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover hashCode and the sample data
commitResults.messageBody:
Codecov flagged the model rework for uncovered lines. The value classes
and Person each had an untested hashCode, and SampleDataUtil had no test
at all despite being rewritten for the new fields.

Add hashCode tests to Company, Role, Linkedin, Name, Phone, Email and
Person, and a SampleDataUtilTest asserting that every sample contact has a
name, that the names are unique so the sample data can be loaded into an
AddressBook, and that some samples deliberately omit optional fields while
at least one is complete.

This takes all seven model classes to full line coverage and SampleDataUtil
from 20% to 93%. The remainder in SampleDataUtil and StringUtil is the
implicit constructor of a utility class, which JaCoCo counts but nothing
can exercise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Git merged this cleanly, but the result did not compile: #60 and #61 added
duplicate phone and email checks to EditCommand that read getPhone().value
and getEmail().value, which this branch changes to return Optional.

Adapt that check to the optional fields rather than reverting it. A person
without a phone number or email now never clashes, since there is no value
of theirs to reuse, and the case-insensitive email comparison is preserved.
Their tests are updated to unwrap the optionals.
